<content>
# EchoGuard

Privacy-preserving, camera-free motion and potential-fall sensing with Wi-Fi
Channel State Information (CSI) from two ESP32 boards.

> **Disclaimer.** EchoGuard is a hackathon research prototype. It is **not a
> medical device**, is **not medically validated**, and must not be relied on
> to detect falls or summon help. No accuracy claims are made.

## Status

| Milestone | State |
| --- | --- |
| 1. CSI connection: firmware, serial parser, recorder, CLI monitor | implemented |
| 2. Live dashboard: signal processing, motion score, local web UI | implemented |
| 3. Calibration and labeled recording | planned |
| 4. Heuristic fall detection | planned |
| 5. Simulation, replay polish, export | planned |

**Not verified yet:** the firmware has not been compiled (ESP-IDF was not
installed on the development machine) and no ESP32 was connected, so the
hardware path (flash, CSI capture, serial streaming) has **not** been tested
end to end. The Python side is tested against the documented Espressif format
using format fixtures (`tests/fixtures/`, not real captures). The dashboard
was exercised by replaying those fixtures and with generated test signals;
the motion score thresholds have not been tuned on real CSI yet.

## Architecture

```
 ESP32 #1 (transmitter)            ESP32 #2 (receiver)              MacBook
 firmware/transmitter     ESP-NOW  firmware/receiver      USB       backend/
 broadcast 100 Hz  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~> CSI callback -> queue  ======>   parser -> buffer
 ch 11, HT40, MCS0                 printer task: CSI_DATA  serial   -> recorder / CLI
 MAC 1a:00:00:00:00:00             lines at 921600 baud             -> processing -> dashboard
```

* Two ESP32s only. No router, no mesh, no internet at runtime.
* The receiver prints the official esp-csi `CSI_DATA` CSV format, so the
  official Espressif tools also work with it.
* A Raspberry Pi can replace the Mac as host (same Python code), but is not required.

## Repository layout

```
firmware/transmitter/   ESP-IDF project (from esp-csi csi_send)
firmware/receiver/      ESP-IDF project (from esp-csi csi_recv)
firmware/flash_helper.sh  guarded build+flash helper (explicit port + confirmation)
backend/                csi_parser, sources (serial/replay), ports, buffer, recorder, cli,
                        config, processing, activity, engine
dashboard/              Flask server (server.py, __main__.py) + static/ offline UI (HTML/CSS/JS)
tests/                  pytest suite + format fixtures
data/                   config.json, recordings/, calibration/, exports/, models/ (gitignored)
```

## macOS setup (host software)

```bash
brew install python@3.11        # if /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.11 is missing
make setup                      # creates .venv and installs pinned requirements.txt
make test                       # runs the unit tests
```

`make setup` prefers Python 3.11 (falls back to 3.12). Python 3.14 is avoided
because binary wheels for some pinned packages may not exist yet. Internet is
only needed for this install step.

No internet? If a local interpreter already has the packages from
`requirements.txt` (numpy, scipy, pandas, pyserial, flask, pytest), build the
venv on top of it without any download:

```bash
make setup-offline                                   # default: ~/miniconda3/bin/python3.12
make setup-offline PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP=/path/to/python3 # any other interpreter
```

This recreates `.venv` with `--system-site-packages` and checks the imports.
Optional ML extras (scikit-learn, joblib, used later for Random Forest
training) are in `requirements-ml.txt`: `make setup-ml`.

## ESP-IDF installation (macOS)

```bash
brew install cmake ninja dfu-util ccache
mkdir -p ~/esp && cd ~/esp
git clone -b v5.5.1 --recursive https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf.git
cd esp-idf && ./install.sh esp32,esp32s3,esp32c3,esp32c6
. ./export.sh                    # run in every new terminal (or add an alias)
idf.py --version
```

See the [ESP-IDF get-started guide](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32/get-started/index.html)
for details. The first receiver build downloads the `esp_csi_gain_ctrl`
component (needs internet once).

## Identify your boards (read-only)

```bash
make ports                                   # lists ports, flags likely ESP32s
esptool.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX chip_id   # prints chip type + MAC, writes nothing
```

`chip_id` resets the board but does not write flash. **Do not connect the third
ESP32 that holds firmware you want to keep**; if it is plugged in, unplug it
before flashing anything. Nothing in this repository flashes automatically.

## Build and flash

Pick the target that `chip_id` reported (`esp32`, `esp32s3`, `esp32c3`, `esp32c6`).

Receiver (CSI source, connected to the Mac):

```bash
. ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh
cd firmware/receiver
idf.py set-target esp32s3                    # use your chip
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbserial-XXXX flash monitor
```

Transmitter (can be powered by any USB supply once flashed):

```bash
cd firmware/transmitter
idf.py set-target esp32                      # use your chip
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY flash monitor
```

Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 (and other boards with only native USB): add the
USB-Serial-JTAG console overlay, otherwise no serial output appears:

```bash
idf.py -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.defaults.usbjtag" set-target esp32s3
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX flash monitor
```

Guarded alternative (read-only chip check, target match, typed confirmation):

```bash
firmware/flash_helper.sh --port /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX --role rx --target esp32s3 --usbjtag
firmware/flash_helper.sh --port /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY --role tx --target esp32
```

More details and all Kconfig options: [firmware/README.md](firmware/README.md).

## Milestone 1 usage

Close `idf.py monitor` first (`Ctrl-]`), then:

```bash
make ports
make monitor                      # PORT=auto; or: make monitor PORT=/dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX
.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli monitor --port auto --record data/recordings/test.csv
.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli monitor --replay data/recordings/test.csv
.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli monitor --replay tests/fixtures/classic_esp32s3_sample.txt --duration 3
```

Once per second the monitor prints connection state, total CSI packets, packet
rate, malformed lines, sequence gaps, RSSI (mean/std), noise floor, CSI length,
chip family, mean amplitude and a sparkline of the 52 valid LLTF subcarrier
amplitudes, plus the device's own `EG_RX_STATS`. Before any packet arrives it
prints `waiting for CSI packets` (no values are invented). Walk between the
boards and the sparkline / mean amplitude should change.

`--port auto` picks the single likely ESP32 port; if several are connected it
listens (read-only) on each for `CSI_DATA` and picks the one that emits it.
The serial source reconnects automatically after unplugging.

Recordings are CSV files with `host_ts_iso,host_ts_unix,raw_line`; replay feeds
the raw lines through the same parser. Raw `idf.py monitor` logs (`.txt`/`.log`)
can be replayed too (at 100 lines/s, since they have no host timestamps).

## Milestone 2: live dashboard

```bash
make dashboard                                   # http://127.0.0.1:8050/ opens in the browser
make dashboard ARGS="--serial auto"              # start reading the receiver right away
.venv/bin/python -m dashboard --serial /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX
.venv/bin/python -m dashboard --replay data/recordings/test.csv --speed 1 --loop
.venv/bin/python -m dashboard --no-browser --port 8599 --replay tests/fixtures/classic_esp32s3_sample.txt
```

In the page, the **Data source** card selects a serial port (`auto` or a
listed `/dev/cu.*` device, baud 921600) or a replay file (recordings under
`data/` and the format fixtures), with speed and loop options. Close
`idf.py monitor` first; only one program can open the port.

Panels:

* **Connection status**: source state, port, reconnects and last error;
  packet rate and counts; RSSI (last, mean, sd), noise floor and mean CSI
  amplitude; malformed lines (by reason), sequence gaps and duplicates;
  a signal-quality badge with the reasons when data is insufficient; the TX/RX
  configuration seen in the packets (chip family, channel, secondary channel,
  bandwidth, CSI length, subcarrier count, TX MAC) and the device's own
  `EG_RX_STATS` / `EG_TX_STATS`.
* **Motion classification**: one of *Empty room / low activity*, *Movement
  detected*, *Rapid movement*, *Potential fall* (set by the fall detector in
  Milestone 4) or *Unknown / insufficient data*, plus the current motion
  score, baseline deviation and thresholds.
* **Live CSI**: scrolling heatmap of the normalised subcarrier amplitudes
  (time left to right, newest at right, with colour scale), mean amplitude,
  motion activity score with the movement / rapid threshold lines, baseline
  deviation, and RSSI over the last 30 s.

A **REPLAY of recorded data** banner is shown during replays (a
**SIMULATED DATA** banner is reserved for the simulation mode). Before data
arrives every field shows `No data yet` / `-`; nothing is invented.

Signal processing (`backend/processing.py`), per packet: the 52 valid LLTF
subcarrier amplitudes (C5/C6: all non-zero subcarriers) are divided by their
mean (removes AGC gain jumps), a Hampel filter replaces impulsive outliers per
subcarrier, and an EMA smooths them. Over a 1 s window it computes the
temporal **variance** (mean per-subcarrier std), the **diff energy** (RMS of
the first difference), the **baseline deviation** (mean z-score of the window
profile against the calibration baseline, or against a slow 30 s adaptive
reference until a calibration exists) and the **motion score**
`0.5 * (variance / noise_var + diff_energy / noise_diff)`; with a calibration
an empty room scores about 1. Data quality is *insufficient* (activity
*Unknown*) when the packet rate is below 20 Hz, the window is less than 70%
covered, the CSI layout changed, or no packet arrived for 1 s. Parameters and
thresholds live in `data/config.json` (created with defaults on first start).
**Until calibration (Milestone 3) the thresholds are uncalibrated defaults**,
so the classification is only indicative.

Framework choice: the dashboard is a small Flask app with a self-contained
HTML/CSS/vanilla-JavaScript page that draws its charts on `<canvas>`. It needs
no CDN or internet (Streamlit/Plotly could not be installed offline and are
not required). The page polls `/api/status`, `/api/series` and `/api/heatmap`
about 2.5 times per second.

**Security note:** the dashboard has **no authentication**. It binds to
`127.0.0.1` by default. `--host 0.0.0.0` (e.g. to view it from another
machine, or on a Raspberry Pi host) prints a warning: anyone who can reach the
address can see the data and change the data source. Only do that on a
trusted network.

## Serial format

Receiver lines follow the official esp-csi format.

Classic ESP32 / ESP32-S3 / ESP32-C3 (25 fields):

```
type,id,mac,rssi,rate,sig_mode,mcs,bandwidth,smoothing,not_sounding,aggregation,stbc,fec_coding,sgi,noise_floor,ampdu_cnt,channel,secondary_channel,local_timestamp,ant,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data
CSI_DATA,0,94:d9:b3:80:8c:81,-30,11,1,6,1,0,1,0,1,0,0,-93,0,13,2,2751923,0,67,0,128,1,"[67,48,4,0,...]"
```

ESP32-C5 / ESP32-C6 (15 fields):

```
type,seq,mac,rssi,rate,noise_floor,fft_gain,agc_gain,channel,local_timestamp,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data
```

* `id` / `seq`: transmitter packet counter (used for loss / gap counting).
* `local_timestamp`: receiver clock in microseconds.
* `len`: number of integers in `data`. With `ECHOGUARD_RX_LLTF_ONLY` (default on
  classic chips) it is 128.
* `first_word`: 1 means the first 4 values (subcarriers 0 and 1) are invalid.
* `data`: interleaved `[imag, real]` per subcarrier; decoded as
  `complex(raw[2k+1], raw[2k])` like the official parser. On classic chips the
  first 64 subcarriers are the LLTF in order 0..31, -32..-1; the 52 valid ones
  are indices 1..26 and 38..63.

EchoGuard additions (one line per second):

```
EG_RX_STATS,<uptime_ms>,<csi_rx_total>,<csi_rx_rate_hz>,<queue_drops>,<seq_gaps>,<last_rssi>
EG_TX_STATS,<uptime_ms>,<sent_ok>,<send_fail>,<rate_hz>
```

## Serial troubleshooting

* **Port names on macOS.** Native USB (XIAO ESP32-S3, ESP32-C3/C6/S3 USB
  port): `/dev/cu.usbmodem*`. USB-UART bridges: `/dev/cu.usbserial-*`,
  `/dev/cu.SLAB_USBtoUART` (CP210x), `/dev/cu.wchusbserial*` (CH34x). Use
  `/dev/cu.*`, not `/dev/tty.*`. `Bluetooth-Incoming-Port` and `debug-console`
  are macOS system ports, never an ESP32.
* **No port appears.** Try another cable (many are charge-only) and another USB
  port/hub. Recent macOS includes CP210x and CH34x drivers; for older systems
  install the vendor driver (Silicon Labs CP210x VCP, WCH CH34x).
* **Cannot connect / download mode.** Hold BOOT, tap RESET (or plug in while
  holding BOOT), then flash. Native-USB boards may re-enumerate under a new
  `usbmodem` name after flashing; re-run `make ports`.
* **Port busy.** Only one program can open a port. Close `idf.py monitor`
  (`Ctrl-]`), the Arduino serial monitor, `screen`, or another EchoGuard
  monitor.
* **Garbage characters.** The receiver UART runs at **921600** baud (`--baud
  921600`, the default). The transmitter uses the ESP-IDF default 115200.
* **No output on XIAO ESP32-S3.** The default config prints to UART0 pins, not
  the USB-C port. Rebuild with `sdkconfig.defaults.usbjtag` (see above).
* **`waiting for CSI packets` but RX stats show 0 Hz.** Check that the
  transmitter is powered and both use the same channel (`ECHOGUARD_*_CHANNEL`).
* **High `queue_drops` or malformed lines.** The serial link is saturated:
  keep `ECHOGUARD_RX_LLTF_ONLY=y`, or lower `ECHOGUARD_TX_RATE_HZ`.

## Tests

```bash
make test
```

Covers parsing of the documented official example lines (both variants),
complex decoding order, LLTF subcarrier selection and masking, malformed line
handling, stats lines, the bounded buffer (rate, sequence gaps with
wraparound), record/replay round trip, serial reconnect (fake serial and
pyserial `loop://`) and port classification. Milestone 2 adds signal
processing (constant vs. perturbed generated streams, Hampel spike
suppression, quality gates, layout changes, NaN masking, calibrated
normalisation), activity mapping, the engine (fixture replay, error handling,
no fabricated values without a source) and the dashboard API (Flask test
client, including rejection of path traversal and invalid ports). Test
signals are generated in the tests and are not real measurements.

"""Parser for the official Espressif esp-csi ``CSI_DATA`` serial line format.

Two variants are printed by ``examples/get-started/csi_recv`` (and by the
EchoGuard receiver firmware, which keeps the same layout):

* classic ESP32 / ESP32-S3 / ESP32-C3, 25 comma separated fields::

    type,id,mac,rssi,rate,sig_mode,mcs,bandwidth,smoothing,not_sounding,
    aggregation,stbc,fec_coding,sgi,noise_floor,ampdu_cnt,channel,
    secondary_channel,local_timestamp,ant,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data

* ESP32-C5 / ESP32-C6 / ESP32-C61, 15 fields::

    type,seq,mac,rssi,rate,noise_floor,fft_gain,agc_gain,channel,
    local_timestamp,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data

``data`` is a quoted JSON-style list of ``len`` signed integers, interleaved
``[imag0, real0, imag1, real1, ...]`` per subcarrier. The official parser
(``tools/csi_data_read_parse.py``) builds ``complex(raw[2k+1], raw[2k])``, i.e.
``real = raw[2k+1]`` and ``imag = raw[2k]``; this module does the same.

On classic chips the first 128 values are the LLTF (64 subcarriers) in the
order subcarrier 0..31 followed by -32..-1. Index 0 is DC; the 52 subcarriers
that carry legacy 20 MHz data/pilots are indices 1..26 and 38..63. When
``first_word`` (first_word_invalid) is 1 the first four bytes, i.e. subcarriers
0 and 1, are invalid and are masked as NaN.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Optional

import numpy as np

CLASSIC_FIELDS = [
    "type", "id", "mac", "rssi", "rate", "sig_mode", "mcs", "bandwidth", "smoothing",
    "not_sounding", "aggregation", "stbc", "fec_coding", "sgi", "noise_floor", "ampdu_cnt",
    "channel", "secondary_channel", "local_timestamp", "ant", "sig_len", "rx_state", "len",
    "first_word", "data",
]
C5C6_FIELDS = [
    "type", "seq", "mac", "rssi", "rate", "noise_floor", "fft_gain", "agc_gain", "channel",
    "local_timestamp", "sig_len", "rx_state", "len", "first_word", "data",
]

CSI_TAG = "CSI_DATA"
FAMILY_CLASSIC = "classic"
FAMILY_C5C6 = "c5c6"

LLTF_SUBCARRIERS = 64
LLTF_VALUES = 2 * LLTF_SUBCARRIERS
#: LLTF subcarrier indices (0..63, order 0..31 then -32..-1) carrying legacy data/pilots.
VALID_LLTF_INDICES = np.array(list(range(1, 27)) + list(range(38, 64)), dtype=np.int64)

_ANSI_RE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[ -/]*[@-~]")
_MAC_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-fA-F]{2}(:[0-9a-fA-F]{2}){5}$")


class ParseError(ValueError):
    """A line that contains ``CSI_DATA`` but cannot be decoded.

    ``reason`` is a short machine readable code (``field_count``,
    ``non_numeric``, ``bad_mac``, ``bad_data``, ``truncated_data``,
    ``len_mismatch``, ``odd_value_count``, ``empty_data``).
    """

    def __init__(self, reason: str, detail: str, line: str = ""):
        super().__init__(f"{reason}: {detail}")
        self.reason = reason
        self.detail = detail
        self.line = line


@dataclass
class CSIPacket:
    """One decoded CSI measurement. Field names follow the official headers."""

    host_ts: Optional[float]
    chip_family: str
    seq: int                      # 'id' (classic) or 'seq' (C5/C6): TX packet counter
    mac: str
    rssi: int
    rate: int
    noise_floor: int
    channel: int
    local_timestamp: int          # receiver clock, microseconds
    sig_len: int
    rx_state: int
    len: int                      # number of int values in 'data'
    first_word_invalid: bool
    raw: list
    csi: np.ndarray               # complex64, one value per subcarrier
    amplitude: np.ndarray         # float32 |csi|
    phase: np.ndarray             # float32 angle(csi), radians
    raw_line: str
    # classic-only header fields (None on C5/C6)
    sig_mode: Optional[int] = None
    mcs: Optional[int] = None
    bandwidth: Optional[int] = None
    smoothing: Optional[int] = None
    not_sounding: Optional[int] = None
    aggregation: Optional[int] = None
    stbc: Optional[int] = None
    fec_coding: Optional[int] = None
    sgi: Optional[int] = None
    ampdu_cnt: Optional[int] = None
    secondary_channel: Optional[int] = None
    ant: Optional[int] = None
    # C5/C6-only header fields (None on classic)
    fft_gain: Optional[int] = None
    agc_gain: Optional[int] = None

    @property
    def n_subcarriers(self) -> int:
        return int(self.csi.shape[0])


@dataclass
class RxStats:
    """``EG_RX_STATS`` line printed once per second by the EchoGuard receiver."""

    uptime_ms: int
    csi_rx_total: int
    csi_rx_rate_hz: float
    queue_drops: int
    seq_gaps: int
    last_rssi: int
    host_ts: Optional[float] = None


@dataclass
class TxStats:
    """``EG_TX_STATS`` line printed once per second by the EchoGuard transmitter."""

    uptime_ms: int
    sent_ok: int
    send_fail: int

class ReplaySource(LineSource):
    """Re-emit recorded lines through the normal pipeline.

    Accepts two formats:

    * EchoGuard recordings written by :class:`backend.recorder.RawRecorder`
      (CSV with ``host_ts_iso,host_ts_unix,raw_line,...``): original relative
      timing is reproduced, scaled by ``speed``.
    * plain raw serial logs (``.txt`` / ``.log``, e.g. ``idf.py monitor``
      captures, test fixtures): no host timestamps exist, so lines are emitted
      at ``line_rate_hz`` (scaled by ``speed``).

    ``speed=0`` means as fast as possible. Yielded ``host_ts`` values follow
    the (scaled) original timeline starting at the replay start time, so rate
    calculations stay meaningful.
    """

    kind = "replay"

    def __init__(self, path, speed: float = 1.0, loop: bool = False, line_rate_hz: float = 100.0) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.speed = float(speed)
        self.loop = loop
        self.line_rate_hz = float(line_rate_hz)
        self.status.port = str(self.path)
        self.recording_format = self._detect_format()
        self.status.extra["format"] = self.recording_format

    def _detect_format(self) -> str:
        with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", newline="") as f:
            first = f.readline()
        return "recording" if first.startswith(",".join(RAW_FIELDS)) else "raw_log"

    def _iter_original(self) -> Iterator[Tuple[float, str]]:
        """Yield (original_relative_seconds, line)."""
        if self.recording_format == "recording":
            with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", newline="") as f:
                t0 = None
                for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                    try:
                        ts = float(row["host_ts_unix"])
                    except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError):
                        continue
                    if t0 is None:
                        t0 = ts
                    yield ts - t0, row.get("raw_line") or ""
        else:
            period = 1.0 / self.line_rate_hz if self.line_rate_hz > 0 else 0.0
            with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                for i, line in enumerate(f):
                    yield i * period, line.rstrip("\r\n")

    def lines(self) -> Iterator[Line]:
        self.status.connected = True
        self.status.connected_since = time.time()
        start = time.time()
        loop_offset = 0.0
        try:
            while not self._stop.is_set():
                last_rel = 0.0
                for rel, line in self._iter_original():
                    if self._stop.is_set():
                        return
                    rel_scaled = (rel / self.speed) if self.speed > 0 else rel
                    last_rel = rel_scaled
                    target = start + loop_offset + rel_scaled
                    if self.speed > 0:
                        delay = target - time.time()
                        if delay > 0 and self._stop.wait(delay):
                            return
                    self.status.lines_read += 1
                    self.status.bytes_read += len(line) + 1
                    yield target, line

SESSION_TAKE_GAP_S = 0.5

class ReplaySource(LineSource):
    """Re-emit recorded lines through the normal pipeline.

    Accepts these inputs:

    * EchoGuard recordings (CSV with ``host_ts_unix`` and ``raw_line``
      columns): :class:`backend.recorder.RawRecorder` files and labeled take
      CSVs from :mod:`backend.recording`. Original relative timing is
      reproduced, scaled by ``speed``. For labeled takes the current
      ``session_id`` / ``take_id`` / ``label`` / ``label_name`` are published in
      ``status.extra`` as ground truth.
    * a session directory (containing ``session.json``): all takes are
      replayed in take order with a short pause between takes.
    * plain raw serial logs (``.txt`` / ``.log``, e.g. ``idf.py monitor``
      captures, test fixtures): no host timestamps exist, so lines are emitted
      at ``line_rate_hz`` (scaled by ``speed``).

    ``speed=0`` means as fast as possible. Yielded ``host_ts`` values follow
    the (scaled) original timeline starting at the replay start time, so rate
    calculations stay meaningful. ``synthetic`` is taken from the session's
    ``session.json`` when one exists (simulated recordings stay marked).
    """

    kind = "replay"

    def __init__(self, path, speed: float = 1.0, loop: bool = False, line_rate_hz: float = 100.0) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.speed = float(speed)
        self.loop = loop
        self.line_rate_hz = float(line_rate_hz)
        self.synthetic = False
        self._files = [self.path]
        self.status.port = str(self.path)
        self.recording_format = self._detect_format()
        self.status.extra["format"] = self.recording_format
        if self.recording_format in ("recording", "session") and self._has_labels:
            for k in GROUND_TRUTH_KEYS:
                self.status.extra[k] = None

    def _detect_format(self) -> str:
        self._has_labels = False
        session_json = None
        if self.path.is_dir():
            session_json = self.path / "session.json"
            if not session_json.is_file():
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"{self.path} is not a session directory (no session.json)")
        elif (self.path.parent / "session.json").is_file():
            session_json = self.path.parent / "session.json"
        if session_json is not None:
            try:
                meta = json.loads(session_json.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                self.synthetic = bool(meta.get("synthetic", False))
            except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError):
                meta = None
            if self.path.is_dir():
                from .recording import Session  # local import: recording imports this package's parser only

                self._files = Session.load(self.path).take_files()
                self.status.extra["takes"] = len(self._files)
                self._has_labels = True
                return "session"
        with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", newline="") as f:
            header = next(csv.reader([f.readline()]), [])
        if "host_ts_unix" in header and "raw_line" in header:
            self._has_labels = "label" in header
            return "recording"
        return "raw_log"

    @staticmethod
    def _iter_csv(path: Path) -> Iterator[Tuple[float, str, dict]]:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", newline="") as f:
            t0 = None
            for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                try:
                    ts = float(row["host_ts_unix"])
                except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError):
                    continue
                if t0 is None:
                    t0 = ts
                yield ts - t0, row.get("raw_line") or "", row

    def _iter_original(self) -> Iterator[Tuple[float, str, Optional[dict]]]:
        """Yield (original_relative_seconds, line, csv_row_or_None)."""
        if self.recording_format == "session":
            offset = 0.0
            for path in self._files:
                last = 0.0
                for rel, line, row in self._iter_csv(path):
                    last = rel
                    yield offset + rel, line, row
                offset += last + SESSION_TAKE_GAP_S
        elif self.recording_format == "recording":
            yield from self._iter_csv(self.path)
        else:
            period = 1.0 / self.line_rate_hz if self.line_rate_hz > 0 else 0.0
            with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                for i, line in enumerate(f):
                    yield i * period, line.rstrip("\r\n"), None

    def lines(self) -> Iterator[Line]:
        self.status.connected = True
        self.status.connected_since = time.time()
        start = time.time()
        loop_offset = 0.0
        extra = self.status.extra
        try:
            while not self._stop.is_set():
                last_rel = 0.0
                for rel, line, row in self._iter_original():
                    if self._stop.is_set():
                        return
                    rel_scaled = (rel / self.speed) if self.speed > 0 else rel
                    last_rel = rel_scaled
                    target = start + loop_offset + rel_scaled
                    if self.speed > 0:
                        delay = target - time.time()
                        if delay > 0 and self._stop.wait(delay):
                            return
                    if row is not None and self._has_labels:
                        label = row.get("label") or None
                        if label != extra.get("label") or row.get("take_id") != extra.get("take_id"):
                            from .recording import LABELS

                            extra["session_id"] = row.get("session_id") or None
                            extra["take_id"] = row.get("take_id") or None
                            extra["label"] = label
                            extra["label_name"] = LABELS.get(label, label)
                    self.status.lines_read += 1
                    self.status.bytes_read += len(line) + 1
                    yield target, line

"""Guided self-calibration: noise levels, baseline profile and motion thresholds.

Workflow (:class:`CalibrationSession`), each step recorded for a fixed span of
packet time while the engine runs:

1. ``empty_baseline`` - empty, stationary room (15-30 s, default 20 s)
2. ``walking``        - a person walks across the sensing area (default 15 s)
3. ``standing_still`` - a person stands still in the area (default 10 s)
4. ``sitting``        - ordinary sitting down / seated (default 10 s)
5. compute            - :func:`compute_calibration`

Frames come from the engine thread (``Engine.add_frame_hook``) together with
``SignalProcessor.last_smoothed`` (the normalised, filtered amplitude profile
that the features and the baseline deviation use). Nothing is driven by the UI
refresh.

Computed values:

* empty-room baseline: per-subcarrier mean and std of the smoothed profile,
* noise levels: median / p95 of variance, diff energy, baseline deviation and
  motion score in the empty room; ``noise_variance`` / ``noise_diff`` (medians)
  become the motion-score normalisation, so a calibrated empty room scores ~1,
* per-step distributions (median, quartiles, p5/p95) of the recomputed
  calibrated motion score and other features, and per-step mean profiles,
* preliminary thresholds from the empty/still p95 and the walking median/p95
  (monotonic ``low < movement < rapid``; falls back to conservative defaults
  with a warning when walking is not clearly separable from stillness).

Calibrations are persisted as ``data/calibration/<sensor_key>.json``, where the
key combines placement, chip family, TX MAC, channel, secondary channel and
CSI length. Calibrations computed from synthetic (simulated) data carry
``synthetic: true`` and a ``__synthetic`` key suffix, and are never applied to
real sources automatically (and not manually either).

These thresholds are preliminary heuristics, not validated detection limits.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import math
import re
import threading
import time
import warnings
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

import numpy as np

from . import __version__
from .config import DATA_DIR, MotionThresholds
from .processing import STD_FLOOR
from .recording import iso, validate_placement, write_json_atomic

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_DIR = DATA_DIR / "calibration"
CALIBRATION_FORMAT = 1
KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,159}$")
SYNTHETIC_SUFFIX = "__synthetic"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StepSpec:
    key: str
    title: str
    instructions: str
    default_s: float
    min_s: float
    max_s: float


STEPS = [
    StepSpec("empty_baseline", "Empty room baseline",
             "Leave the sensing area (or the room) and keep everything still: no people, pets, fans or "
             "moving curtains between or near the two boards.", 20.0, 15.0, 30.0),
    StepSpec("walking", "Walking",
             "Walk back and forth across the sensing area, crossing the line between the two boards, "
             "at a normal pace.", 15.0, 5.0, 60.0),
    StepSpec("standing_still", "Standing still",
             "Stand still in the middle of the sensing area. Breathe normally, do not move your arms.",
             10.0, 5.0, 60.0),
    StepSpec("sitting", "Ordinary sitting",
             "Sit down on a chair in the sensing area as you normally would and stay seated.",
             10.0, 5.0, 60.0),
]
STEP_KEYS = [s.key for s in STEPS]
STEP_BY_KEY = {s.key: s for s in STEPS}

#: A step needs this fraction of frames with sufficient data quality ...
MIN_OK_FRACTION = 0.8
#: ... and at least this many good frames (or half the expected frames).
MIN_OK_FRAMES = 20
#: Walking median must exceed the quiet (empty/still) p95 by this factor.
SEPARATION_RATIO = 1.5
#: Minimum relative gaps enforced between thresholds.
MOVEMENT_OVER_LOW = 1.1
RAPID_OVER_MOVEMENT = 1.2
#: Floor for the noise references (normalised amplitude units).
NOISE_FLOOR = 1e-6
FEATURES = ("motion_score", "variance", "diff_energy", "baseline_deviation")


class CalibrationError(ValueError):
    """Invalid request, state, or data that cannot be calibrated (HTTP 400)."""


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
def _slug_part(value) -> str:
    s = re.sub(r"[^0-9a-z]", "", str(value).lower())
    return s or "na"


def sensor_part(sensor: Optional[dict], synthetic: bool = False) -> Optional[str]:
    """Placement-independent part of the calibration key (None if unknown)."""
    if not sensor or not sensor.get("chip_family"):
        return None
    sec = sensor.get("secondary_channel")
    part = (f"{_slug_part(sensor.get('chip_family'))}_{_slug_part(sensor.get('tx_mac') or 'unknown')}"
            f"_ch{_slug_part(sensor.get('channel'))}-{_slug_part(sec if sec is not None else 'na')}"
            f"_len{_slug_part(sensor.get('csi_len'))}")
    return part + (SYNTHETIC_SUFFIX if synthetic else "")


def sensor_key(sensor: dict, placement: str, synthetic: bool = False) -> str:
    """``<placement>__<chip>_<txmac>_ch<ch>-<sec>_len<len>[__synthetic]``."""
    part = sensor_part(sensor, synthetic)
    if part is None:
        raise CalibrationError("sensor configuration unknown (no CSI packets seen yet)")
    return f"{validate_placement(placement)}__{part}"


def validate_key(key) -> str:
    if not isinstance(key, str) or not KEY_RE.match(key):
        raise CalibrationError("invalid calibration key")
    return key


def _stats(values) -> Optional[dict]:
    a = np.asarray([v for v in values if v is not None], dtype=float)
    a = a[np.isfinite(a)]
    if a.size == 0:
        return None
    p = np.percentile(a, [5, 25, 50, 75, 95])
    return {"n": int(a.size), "min": float(a.min()), "p05": float(p[0]), "p25": float(p[1]), "median": float(p[2]),
            "p75": float(p[3]), "p95": float(p[4]), "max": float(a.max()), "mean": float(a.mean())}


def _profile_stats(profiles: list):
    if not profiles:
        return None, None
    P = np.vstack(profiles).astype(float)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
        return np.nanmean(P, axis=0), np.nanstd(P, axis=0)


def _json_list(arr) -> list:
    return [round(float(v), 6) if v is not None and math.isfinite(v) else None for v in np.asarray(arr, dtype=float)]


def _to_array(values) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.array([np.nan if v is None else v for v in values], dtype=float)


# -------------------------------------------------------------- step data
@dataclass
class StepData:
    key: str
    duration_s: float
    status: str = "pending"            # pending | recording | done | failed
    failure: Optional[str] = None
    t0: Optional[float] = None
    t_last: Optional[float] = None
    wall_start: Optional[float] = None
    total: int = 0
    ok: int = 0
    reasons: Counter = field(default_factory=Counter)
    features: dict = field(default_factory=lambda: {k: [] for k in FEATURES})
    profiles: list = field(default_factory=list)
    layout: Optional[tuple] = None
    sensor: Optional[dict] = None
    synthetic: Optional[bool] = None
    source_kind: Optional[str] = None
    problems: list = field(default_factory=list)
    last_quality: Optional[dict] = None

    @property
    def elapsed_s(self) -> float:
        if self.t0 is None or self.t_last is None:
            return 0.0
        return max(0.0, self.t_last - self.t0)

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        spec = STEP_BY_KEY[self.key]
        return {
            "key": self.key, "title": spec.title, "instructions": spec.instructions,
            "duration_s": self.duration_s, "status": self.status, "failure": self.failure,
            "elapsed_s": round(self.elapsed_s, 2), "frames": self.total, "ok_frames": self.ok,
            "ok_fraction": round(self.ok / self.total, 3) if self.total else None,
            "top_reasons": [{"reason": r, "count": c} for r, c in self.reasons.most_common(3)],
            "last_quality": self.last_quality,
        }


def step_problems(sd: StepData, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0) -> list:
    """Reasons why a step's data is insufficient (empty list = OK)."""
    problems = list(sd.problems)
    if sd.total == 0:
        return problems + ["no motion frames were received (is a data source running?)"]
    frac = sd.ok / sd.total
    min_ok = max(MIN_OK_FRAMES, int(0.5 * sd.duration_s * max(frame_rate_hz, 1.0)))
    top = ", ".join(f"{r} x{c}" for r, c in sd.reasons.most_common(3))
    if frac < MIN_OK_FRACTION:
        problems.append(f"only {frac:.0%} of frames had sufficient data quality (need {MIN_OK_FRACTION:.0%})"
                        + (f"; main reasons: {top}" if top else ""))
    if sd.ok < min_ok:
        problems.append(f"only {sd.ok} frames with sufficient quality (need at least {min_ok})")
    if sd.elapsed_s < 0.9 * sd.duration_s:
        problems.append(f"covered {sd.elapsed_s:.1f} s of {sd.duration_s:g} s")
    if sd.key == "empty_baseline" and len(sd.profiles) < min_ok:
        problems.append("not enough amplitude profiles for the baseline")
    return problems


# --------------------------------------------------------------- compute
def compute_calibration(steps: dict, placement: str, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0,
                        defaults: Optional[MotionThresholds] = None, now: Optional[float] = None) -> dict:
    """Derive baseline, noise levels and thresholds from recorded steps.

    ``steps`` maps step keys to :class:`StepData`. Raises
    :class:`CalibrationError` (with every reason) when a step is missing or its
    data quality was insufficient.
    """
    defaults = defaults or MotionThresholds()
    problems = []
    for key in STEP_KEYS:
        sd = steps.get(key)
        if sd is None or sd.total == 0:
            problems.append(f"{STEP_BY_KEY[key].title}: not recorded")
            continue
        for p in step_problems(sd, frame_rate_hz):
            problems.append(f"{STEP_BY_KEY[key].title}: {p}")
    if problems:
        raise CalibrationError("cannot compute calibration: " + "; ".join(problems))

    empty = steps["empty_baseline"]
    layouts = {steps[k].layout for k in STEP_KEYS}
    if len(layouts) != 1:
        raise CalibrationError("cannot compute calibration: the CSI layout differs between steps")
    warnings_out = []

    ev = np.asarray(empty.features["variance"], dtype=float)
    ed = np.asarray(empty.features["diff_energy"], dtype=float)
    noise_variance = float(np.median(ev))
    noise_diff = float(np.median(ed))
    if noise_variance < NOISE_FLOOR or noise_diff < NOISE_FLOOR:
        warnings_out.append("empty-room noise is essentially zero; noise references were floored "
                            f"at {NOISE_FLOOR:g} (is the signal real and varying?)")
    noise_variance = max(noise_variance, NOISE_FLOOR)
    noise_diff = max(noise_diff, NOISE_FLOOR)

    base_mean, base_std = _profile_stats(empty.profiles)

    def deviation(profile):
        ok = np.isfinite(profile) & np.isfinite(base_mean) & np.isfinite(base_std)
        if not ok.any():
            return None
        return float(np.mean(np.abs(profile[ok] - base_mean[ok]) / np.maximum(base_std[ok], STD_FLOOR)))

    step_out = {}
    scores = {}
    for key in STEP_KEYS:
        sd = steps[key]
        v = np.asarray(sd.features["variance"], dtype=float)
        d = np.asarray(sd.features["diff_energy"], dtype=float)
        s = 0.5 * (v / noise_variance + d / noise_diff)
        scores[key] = s
        devs = [deviation(p) for p in sd.profiles]
        pm, ps = _profile_stats(sd.profiles)
        step_out[key] = {
            "title": STEP_BY_KEY[key].title,
            "duration_s": sd.duration_s,
            "elapsed_s": round(sd.elapsed_s, 2),
            "frames": sd.total,
            "ok_frames": sd.ok,
            "ok_fraction": round(sd.ok / sd.total, 3),
            "stats": {
                "motion_score": _stats(s.tolist()),
                "variance": _stats(sd.features["variance"]),
                "diff_energy": _stats(sd.features["diff_energy"]),
                "baseline_deviation": _stats(devs),
                "motion_score_uncalibrated": _stats(sd.features["motion_score"]),
            },
            "profile_mean": _json_list(pm) if pm is not None else [],
            "profile_std": _json_list(ps) if ps is not None else [],
        }

    q = lambda key, pct: float(np.percentile(scores[key], pct))  # noqa: E731
    quiet_p95 = max(q("empty_baseline", 95), q("standing_still", 95))
    walk_med = q("walking", 50)
    walk_p95 = q("walking", 95)
    separable = walk_med >= SEPARATION_RATIO * quiet_p95
    if separable:
        gap = walk_med - quiet_p95
        low = quiet_p95 + 0.25 * gap
        movement = quiet_p95 + 0.5 * gap
        rapid = max(1.5 * walk_p95, 2.0 * movement)
    else:
        warnings_out.append(
            f"walking is not clearly separable from the empty room / standing still (walking median "
            f"{walk_med:.2f} vs quiet p95 {quiet_p95:.2f}, need x{SEPARATION_RATIO:g}); using conservative "
            "default thresholds. Check the board placement and that the person crossed the line between "
            "the boards, then recalibrate.")
        low = max(defaults.low, 1.2 * quiet_p95)
        movement = max(defaults.movement, 1.5 * low)
        rapid = max(defaults.rapid, 2.0 * movement)
    if movement < MOVEMENT_OVER_LOW * low:
        movement = MOVEMENT_OVER_LOW * low
        warnings_out.append("movement threshold raised to keep it above the stillness threshold")
    if rapid < RAPID_OVER_MOVEMENT * movement:
        rapid = RAPID_OVER_MOVEMENT * movement
        warnings_out.append("rapid threshold raised to keep it above the movement threshold")
    if q("sitting", 50) >= rapid:
        warnings_out.append("ordinary sitting scored above the rapid-movement threshold; rapid movement may be "
                            "flagged during normal sitting")

    now = time.time() if now is None else now
    noise = {f: step_out["empty_baseline"]["stats"][f] for f in ("variance", "diff_energy", "baseline_deviation")}
    noise["motion_score"] = step_out["empty_baseline"]["stats"]["motion_score"]
    family, width = empty.layout
    synthetic = any(bool(steps[k].synthetic) for k in STEP_KEYS)
    return {
        "format": CALIBRATION_FORMAT,
        "kind": "echoguard-calibration",
        "placement": validate_placement(placement),
        "created": iso(now),
        "created_unix": now,
        "app_version": __version__,
        "source_kind": empty.source_kind,
        "synthetic": synthetic,
        "sensor": empty.sensor,
        "durations": {k: steps[k].duration_s for k in STEP_KEYS},
        "baseline": {"chip_family": family, "n_subcarriers": width,
                     "mean_profile": _json_list(base_mean), "std_profile": _json_list(base_std)},
        "noise_variance": noise_variance,
        "noise_diff": noise_diff,
        "noise": noise,
        "thresholds": {"low": round(low, 4), "movement": round(movement, 4), "rapid": round(rapid, 4),
                       "calibrated": True},
        "separable": bool(separable),
        "quiet_p95": quiet_p95,
        "walking_median": walk_med,
        "walking_p95": walk_p95,
        "warnings": warnings_out,
        "steps": step_out,
        "note": "Preliminary heuristic thresholds from one calibration run; not validated detection limits.",
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------- session
class CalibrationSession:
    """State machine for one guided calibration. Not thread-safe by itself
    (the :class:`CalibrationManager` holds a lock around every call)."""

    def __init__(self, placement: str, durations: Optional[dict] = None, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0,
                 clock=time.time, defaults: Optional[MotionThresholds] = None) -> None:
        self.placement = validate_placement(placement)
        self.frame_rate_hz = float(frame_rate_hz)
        self.clock = clock
        self.defaults = defaults
        durations = durations or {}
        if not isinstance(durations, dict):
            raise CalibrationError("durations must be an object")
        unknown = set(durations) - set(STEP_KEYS)
        if unknown:
            raise CalibrationError(f"unknown calibration steps: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
        self.steps = {}
        for spec in STEPS:
            d = durations.get(spec.key, spec.default_s)
            if isinstance(d, bool) or not isinstance(d, (int, float)) or not (spec.min_s <= d <= spec.max_s):
                raise CalibrationError(f"{spec.title} duration must be {spec.min_s:g}-{spec.max_s:g} s")
            self.steps[spec.key] = StepData(spec.key, float(d))
        self.state = "ready"           # ready | recording | computed | failed | cancelled
        self.step_index = 0
        self.result: Optional[dict] = None
        self.error: Optional[str] = None
        self.created = clock()

    @property
    def current(self) -> Optional[StepData]:
        if 0 <= self.step_index < len(STEPS):
            return self.steps[STEP_KEYS[self.step_index]]
        return None

    def start_step(self) -> None:
        if self.state != "ready" or self.current is None:
            raise CalibrationError(f"cannot start a step in state '{self.state}'")
        sd = self.current
        self.steps[sd.key] = StepData(sd.key, sd.duration_s, status="recording", wall_start=self.clock())
        self.state = "recording"

    def add_frame(self, frame, profile, layout, sensor=None, synthetic=None, source_kind=None) -> None:
        """Engine thread: one motion frame plus the current smoothed profile."""
        if self.state != "recording":
            return
        sd = self.current
        if sd.t0 is None:
            sd.t0 = frame.ts
            sd.layout = layout
            sd.sensor, sd.synthetic, sd.source_kind = sensor, synthetic, source_kind
            ref = self.steps["empty_baseline"]
            if sd.key != "empty_baseline" and ref.status == "done":
                if layout != ref.layout or (sensor_part(sensor) != sensor_part(ref.sensor)) or synthetic != ref.synthetic:
                    sd.problems.append("the sensor configuration or source differs from the empty-room baseline")
                    self._finish_step()
                    return
        elif layout != sd.layout:
            sd.problems.append("the CSI subcarrier layout changed during the step")
            self._finish_step()
            return
        sd.t_last = frame.ts
        sd.total += 1
        sd.last_quality = {"ok": bool(frame.quality_ok), "reasons": list(frame.quality_reasons)}
        feats = (frame.motion_score, frame.variance, frame.diff_energy, frame.baseline_deviation)
        if frame.quality_ok and frame.variance is not None and frame.diff_energy is not None:
            sd.ok += 1
            for name, val in zip(FEATURES, feats):
                sd.features[name].append(val)
            if profile is not None and layout is not None and np.size(profile) == layout[1]:
                sd.profiles.append(np.array(profile, dtype=float))
        else:
            for r in frame.quality_reasons or ["features unavailable"]:
                sd.reasons[r.split(":", 1)[0]] += 1
        if sd.elapsed_s >= sd.duration_s:
            self._finish_step()

    def check_timeout(self, source_ended: bool = False) -> None:
        """Wall-clock guard: end a step that receives no (or too little) data."""
        if self.state != "recording":
            return
        sd = self.current
        waited = self.clock() - (sd.wall_start or self.clock())
        if source_ended or waited > 2.0 * sd.duration_s + 15.0:
            sd.problems.append("the data source ended" if source_ended else "timed out waiting for data")
            self._finish_step()

    def _finish_step(self) -> None:
        sd = self.current
        problems = step_problems(sd, self.frame_rate_hz)
        if problems:
            sd.status = "failed"
            sd.failure = "; ".join(problems)
            self.state = "ready"          # redo the same step
            return
        sd.status = "done"
        sd.failure = None
        self._advance()

    def _advance(self) -> None:
        pending = [i for i, k in enumerate(STEP_KEYS) if self.steps[k].status != "done"]
        if pending:
            self.step_index = pending[0]
            self.state = "ready"
            return
        self.step_index = len(STEPS)
        self.compute()

    def compute(self) -> dict:
        try:
            self.result = compute_calibration(self.steps, self.placement, self.frame_rate_hz, self.defaults,
                                              now=self.clock())
        except CalibrationError as e:
            self.result = None
            self.error = str(e)
            self.state = "failed"
            raise
        self.error = None
        self.state = "computed"
        return self.result

    def cancel_step(self) -> None:
        if self.state != "recording":
            raise CalibrationError("no step is being recorded")
        sd = self.current
        self.steps[sd.key] = StepData(sd.key, sd.duration_s)
        self.state = "ready"

    def redo(self, key: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        if self.state == "cancelled":
            raise CalibrationError("calibration was cancelled; start a new one")
        if self.state == "recording":
            raise CalibrationError("cancel the running step first")
        if key is None:
            if self.current is not None:
                key = self.current.key
            else:
                key = STEP_KEYS[-1]
        if key not in self.steps:
            raise CalibrationError(f"step must be one of: {', '.join(STEP_KEYS)}")
        old = self.steps[key]
        self.steps[key] = StepData(key, old.duration_s)
        self.step_index = STEP_KEYS.index(key)
        self.result = None
        self.error = None
        self.state = "ready"

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        self.state = "cancelled"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        cur = self.current
        return {
            "placement": self.placement,
            "state": self.state,
            "step_index": self.step_index,
            "current_step": cur.key if cur is not None else None,
            "steps": [self.steps[k].summary() for k in STEP_KEYS],
            "result": self.result,
            "error": self.error,
        }


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- store
class CalibrationStore:
    """JSON calibration files in ``root`` (``data/calibration`` by default)."""

    def __init__(self, root: Path = DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_DIR) -> None:
        self.root = Path(root)

    def path_for(self, key: str) -> Path:
        validate_key(key)
        p = (self.root / f"{key}.json").resolve()
        if p.parent != self.root.resolve():
            raise CalibrationError("invalid calibration key")
        return p

    def save(self, result: dict) -> Path:
        key = validate_key(result.get("key"))
        path = self.path_for(key)
        write_json_atomic(path, result)
        return path

    def load(self, key: str) -> dict:
        path = self.path_for(key)
        try:
            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except FileNotFoundError:
            raise CalibrationError("calibration not found") from None
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
            raise CalibrationError(f"cannot read calibration {key}: {e}") from None
        if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("kind") != "echoguard-calibration":
            raise CalibrationError(f"{path.name} is not an EchoGuard calibration")
        data["key"] = key
        return data

    def delete(self, key: str) -> None:
        path = self.path_for(key)
        if not path.is_file():
            raise CalibrationError("calibration not found")
        path.unlink()

    def list(self) -> list:
        out = []
        if not self.root.is_dir():
            return out
        for p in self.root.glob("*.json"):
            if not KEY_RE.match(p.stem):
                continue
            try:
                d = self.load(p.stem)
            except CalibrationError as e:
                log.warning("skipping %s: %s", p.name, e)
                continue
            out.append(summary(d))
        out.sort(key=lambda s: s.get("created_unix") or 0, reverse=True)
        return out

    def find_match(self, sensor: Optional[dict], synthetic: bool, placement: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[dict]:
        """Newest calibration for this sensor configuration (preferring
        ``placement``). Synthetic calibrations only match synthetic sources."""
        part = sensor_part(sensor, synthetic)
        if part is None:
            return None
        cands = [s for s in self.list() if s["key"].split("__", 1)[-1] == part
                 and bool(s.get("synthetic")) == bool(synthetic)]
        if not cands:
            return None
        if placement:
            same = [s for s in cands if s.get("placement") == placement]
            cands = same or cands
        return self.load(cands[0]["key"])


def summary(d: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        "key": d.get("key"), "placement": d.get("placement"), "name": display_name(d),
        "created": d.get("created"), "created_unix": d.get("created_unix"),
        "synthetic": bool(d.get("synthetic", False)), "source_kind": d.get("source_kind"),
        "sensor": d.get("sensor"), "thresholds": d.get("thresholds"), "separable": d.get("separable"),
        "warnings": d.get("warnings", []),
    }


def display_name(d: dict) -> str:
    created = d.get("created_unix")
    when = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", time.localtime(created)) if isinstance(created, (int, float)) else "?"
    return f"{d.get('placement') or 'calibration'} ({when}){' [SYNTHETIC]' if d.get('synthetic') else ''}"


# --------------------------------------------------------------- manager
class CalibrationManager:
    """Connects calibration sessions and stored calibrations to an Engine.

    Registers an engine frame hook that (a) feeds the running calibration step
    and (b) auto-loads the newest stored calibration matching the detected
    sensor configuration (synthetic only for synthetic sources). Guarded by a
    lock: the hook runs in the engine thread, the API in request threads.
    """

    def __init__(self, engine, store: Optional[CalibrationStore] = None, auto_load: bool = True,
                 clock=time.time) -> None:
        self.engine = engine
        self.store = store or CalibrationStore()
        self.auto_load = auto_load
        self.clock = clock
        self._lock = threading.RLock()
        self.session: Optional[CalibrationSession] = None
        self.placement: Optional[str] = None
        self.last_auto: Optional[dict] = None
        self._seen = None
        engine.add_frame_hook(self._on_frame)

    # ----------------------------------------------------- engine thread
    def _on_frame(self, frame, activity) -> None:
        eng = self.engine
        sensor = eng.sensor_config()
        synthetic = bool(eng.synthetic)
        proc = eng.processor
        profile = proc.last_smoothed
        layout = proc.layout
        with self._lock:
            marker = (eng.started_at, sensor_part(sensor, synthetic))
            if self.auto_load and marker != self._seen and marker[1] is not None:
                self._seen = marker
                try:
                    self._auto_select(sensor, synthetic)
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - never break acquisition
                    log.exception("calibration auto-load failed")
            if self.session is not None:
                self.session.add_frame(frame, None if profile is None else profile.copy(), layout,
                                       sensor=sensor, synthetic=synthetic, source_kind=eng.source_kind)

    def _auto_select(self, sensor: dict, synthetic: bool) -> None:
        match = self.store.find_match(sensor, synthetic, placement=self.placement)
        current = self.engine.calibration_info
        if match is not None:
            if current is None or current.get("key") != match["key"]:
                self._apply(match, auto=True)
                self.last_auto = {"time": self.clock(), "action": "loaded", "key": match["key"]}
            return
        if current is not None:
            if current.get("sensor_part") != sensor_part(sensor, synthetic) or bool(current.get("synthetic")) != synthetic:
                self.engine.clear_calibration()
                self.last_auto = {"time": self.clock(), "action": "cleared", "key": current.get("key"),
                                  "reason": "the active calibration does not match the detected sensor configuration"}
                return
        self.last_auto = {"time": self.clock(), "action": "none", "key": None}

    def _apply(self, data: dict, auto: bool = False) -> None:
        b = data.get("baseline") or {}
        mean, std = _to_array(b.get("mean_profile") or []), _to_array(b.get("std_profile") or [])
        if mean.size == 0 or mean.shape != std.shape:
            raise CalibrationError("calibration file has no valid baseline profile")
        th = data.get("thresholds") or {}
        try:
            low, mov, rap = float(th["low"]), float(th["movement"]), float(th["rapid"])
        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            raise CalibrationError("calibration file has no valid thresholds") from None
        if not (0 < low < mov < rap):
            raise CalibrationError("calibration thresholds must satisfy 0 < low < movement < rapid")
        info = {"key": data.get("key"), "name": display_name(data), "created": data.get("created"),
                "synthetic": bool(data.get("synthetic", False)), "auto_loaded": auto,
                "sensor_part": sensor_part(data.get("sensor"), bool(data.get("synthetic", False)))}
        self.engine.apply_calibration(mean, std, data.get("noise_variance"), data.get("noise_diff"),
                                      {"low": low, "movement": mov, "rapid": rap}, info)
        if data.get("placement"):
            self.placement = data["placement"]

    # ------------------------------------------------------- API (requests)
    def start(self, placement: str, durations: Optional[dict] = None) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            if self.session is not None and self.session.state == "recording":
                raise CalibrationError("a calibration step is running; cancel it first")
            self.session = CalibrationSession(placement, durations,
                                              frame_rate_hz=self.engine.config.processing.frame_rate_hz,
                                              clock=self.clock, defaults=self.engine._base_thresholds)
            return self.state()

    def _require_session(self) -> CalibrationSession:
        if self.session is None or self.session.state == "cancelled":
            raise CalibrationError("no calibration in progress; start one first")
        return self.session

    def step_start(self) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            s = self._require_session()
            eng = self.engine
            st = eng.source_status
            if not eng.running or st is None or st.finished:
                raise CalibrationError("no data source is running; connect the receiver (or start a replay) first")
            if eng.source_kind == "live" and not st.connected:
                raise CalibrationError("the serial source is disconnected")
            s.start_step()
            return self.state()

    def step_cancel(self) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            self._require_session().cancel_step()
            return self.state()

    def step_redo(self, key: Optional[str] = None) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            self._require_session().redo(key)
            return self.state()

    def cancel(self) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            self._require_session().cancel()
            self.session = None
            return self.state()

    def save(self) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            s = self._require_session()
            if s.state != "computed" or s.result is None:
                raise CalibrationError("nothing to save: finish all calibration steps first")
            result = dict(s.result)
            if result.get("sensor") is None:
                raise CalibrationError("sensor configuration unknown; cannot key the calibration")
            result["key"] = sensor_key(result["sensor"], s.placement, bool(result.get("synthetic")))
            path = self.store.save(result)
            self._apply(result)
            self.placement = s.placement
            s.result = result
            s.state = "saved"
            return {"key": result["key"], "path": path.name, "calibration": summary(result)}

    def load(self, key: str) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            data = self.store.load(key)
            eng = self.engine
            if eng.source_kind is not None and bool(data.get("synthetic")) and not eng.synthetic:
                raise CalibrationError("this calibration was computed from SYNTHETIC data and cannot be used "
                                       "with real CSI")
            warnings_out = []
            sensor = eng.sensor_config()
            if sensor is not None and sensor_part(sensor, bool(eng.synthetic)) != sensor_part(
                    data.get("sensor"), bool(data.get("synthetic"))):
                warnings_out.append("this calibration was made for a different sensor configuration")
            self._apply(data)
            return {"key": key, "calibration": summary(data), "warnings": warnings_out}

    def delete(self, key: str) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            path = self.store.path_for(key)
            if not path.is_file():
                raise CalibrationError("calibration not found")
            current = self.engine.calibration_info
            if current is not None and current.get("key") == key:
                self.engine.clear_calibration()
            self.store.delete(key)
            return {"key": key}

    def clear(self) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            self.engine.clear_calibration()
            return self.state()

    def state(self) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            s = self.session
            if s is not None:
                st = self.engine.source_status
                ended = s.state == "recording" and (st is None or st.finished or not self.engine.running)
                s.check_timeout(source_ended=ended)
            return {
                "session": s.to_dict() if s is not None else None,
                "active": self.engine.calibration_info,
                "placement": self.placement,
                "last_auto": self.last_auto,
                "step_specs": [{"key": p.key, "title": p.title, "instructions": p.instructions,
                                "default_s": p.default_s, "min_s": p.min_s, "max_s": p.max_s} for p in STEPS],
            }

"""Calibration tests with generated (numpy) CSI streams - not real measurements."""

import json

import numpy as np
import pytest

from backend.calibration import (STEP_KEYS, STEPS, CalibrationError, CalibrationManager, CalibrationSession,
                                 CalibrationStore, compute_calibration, sensor_key, sensor_part)
from backend.config import ProcessingConfig
from backend.engine import Engine
from backend.processing import SignalProcessor
from backend.sources import ReplaySource
from csi_synth import TX_MAC, classic_line, classic_packet, stream

SENSOR = {"tx_mac": TX_MAC, "channel": 11, "secondary_channel": 2, "chip_family": "classic", "csi_len": 128,
          "n_subcarriers": 52}

# step -> generated stream parameters (relative multipath perturbation, noise)
SEPARABLE = {
    "empty_baseline": dict(noise=0.4, perturb=0.0),
    "walking": dict(noise=0.4, perturb=0.12, perturb_hz=1.2),
    "standing_still": dict(noise=0.4, perturb=0.004, perturb_hz=0.3),
    "sitting": dict(noise=0.4, perturb=0.03, perturb_hz=0.8),
}
INSEPARABLE = {k: dict(noise=0.4, perturb=0.0) for k in STEP_KEYS}
DURATIONS = {"empty_baseline": 15, "walking": 5, "standing_still": 5, "sitting": 5}


class Feeder:
    """Runs generated packets through a real SignalProcessor and hands each
    frame + smoothed profile to the session (like the engine hook does)."""

    def __init__(self, session, rate_hz=100.0, synthetic=False):
        self.session = session
        self.proc = SignalProcessor(ProcessingConfig())
        self.t = 1000.0
        self.rate = rate_hz
        self.synthetic = synthetic
        self.seed = 0

    def run(self, seconds, **kw):
        n = int(seconds * self.rate)
        self.seed += 1
        for ts, amps in stream(n, rate_hz=self.rate, t0=self.t, seed=self.seed, **kw):
            frame = self.proc.process(classic_packet(amps, ts))
            if frame is not None:
                self.session.add_frame(frame, self.proc.last_smoothed, self.proc.layout, sensor=SENSOR,
                                       synthetic=self.synthetic, source_kind="replay")
        self.t += n / self.rate + 0.01


def run_all(session, feeder, params, extra_s=0.6):
    for key in STEP_KEYS:
        assert session.current.key == key
        session.start_step()
        feeder.run(session.steps[key].duration_s + extra_s, **params[key])
    return session


def test_step_definitions():
    assert [s.key for s in STEPS] == ["empty_baseline", "walking", "standing_still", "sitting"]
    empty = STEPS[0]
    assert (empty.min_s, empty.default_s, empty.max_s) == (15, 20, 30)
    s = CalibrationSession("Living room")
    assert s.placement == "living-room"
    assert s.steps["empty_baseline"].duration_s == 20
    with pytest.raises(CalibrationError):
        CalibrationSession("x", {"empty_baseline": 10})
    with pytest.raises(CalibrationError):
        CalibrationSession("x", {"empty_baseline": 31})
    with pytest.raises(CalibrationError):
        CalibrationSession("x", {"bogus": 10})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        CalibrationSession("../etc")


def test_separable_streams_give_ordered_thresholds():
    s = CalibrationSession("lab", DURATIONS)
    run_all(s, Feeder(s), SEPARABLE)
    assert s.state == "computed", s.error
    r = s.result
    th = r["thresholds"]
    assert 0 < th["low"] < th["movement"] < th["rapid"]
    assert th["calibrated"] is True
    assert r["separable"] is True
    assert not any("not clearly separable" in w for w in r["warnings"])
    st = r["steps"]
    empty_med = st["empty_baseline"]["stats"]["motion_score"]["median"]
    walk_med = st["walking"]["stats"]["motion_score"]["median"]
    assert 0.7 < empty_med < 1.5          # calibrated empty room scores about 1
    assert walk_med > th["movement"] > st["empty_baseline"]["stats"]["motion_score"]["p95"]
    assert st["standing_still"]["stats"]["motion_score"]["median"] < th["movement"]
    assert len(r["baseline"]["mean_profile"]) == 52 == len(r["baseline"]["std_profile"])
    assert r["noise_variance"] > 0 and r["noise_diff"] > 0
    assert r["noise"]["variance"]["p95"] >= r["noise"]["variance"]["median"]
    assert r["synthetic"] is False and r["sensor"] == SENSOR
    json.dumps(r)


def test_inseparable_data_warns_and_falls_back():
    s = CalibrationSession("lab", DURATIONS)
    run_all(s, Feeder(s), INSEPARABLE)
    assert s.state == "computed", s.error
    r = s.result
    assert r["separable"] is False
    assert any("not clearly separable" in w for w in r["warnings"])
    th = r["thresholds"]
    assert 0 < th["low"] < th["movement"] < th["rapid"]
    assert th["movement"] >= 2.5 and th["rapid"] >= 6.0


def test_insufficient_quality_refuses():
    s = CalibrationSession("lab", DURATIONS)
    f = Feeder(s, rate_hz=10.0)                 # below the 20 Hz quality gate
    s.start_step()
    f.run(16, **SEPARABLE["empty_baseline"])
    sd = s.steps["empty_baseline"]
    assert sd.status == "failed"
    assert "sufficient data quality" in sd.failure and "low_packet_rate" in sd.failure
    assert s.state == "ready" and s.current.key == "empty_baseline"
    with pytest.raises(CalibrationError, match="cannot compute"):
        compute_calibration(s.steps, "lab")
    # redo with good data proceeds to the next step
    s.start_step()
    Feeder(s).run(15.6, **SEPARABLE["empty_baseline"])
    assert s.steps["empty_baseline"].status == "done"
    assert s.current.key == "walking"


def test_redo_and_cancel_step():
    s = CalibrationSession("lab", DURATIONS)
    f = Feeder(s)
    s.start_step()
    f.run(3, **SEPARABLE["empty_baseline"])
    s.cancel_step()
    assert s.state == "ready" and s.steps["empty_baseline"].total == 0
    run_all(s, f, SEPARABLE)
    assert s.state == "computed"
    s.redo("walking")
    assert s.state == "ready" and s.current.key == "walking" and s.result is None
    s.start_step()
    f.run(5.6, **SEPARABLE["walking"])
    assert s.state == "computed"            # the other steps are kept


def test_timeout_without_data():
    now = [0.0]
    s = CalibrationSession("lab", DURATIONS, clock=lambda: now[0])
    s.start_step()
    now[0] = 100.0
    s.check_timeout()
    assert s.steps["empty_baseline"].status == "failed"
    assert "no motion frames" in s.steps["empty_baseline"].failure


def test_sensor_key():
    k = sensor_key(SENSOR, "Living room")
    assert k == "living-room__classic_1a0000000000_ch11-2_len128"
    assert sensor_key(SENSOR, "x", synthetic=True).endswith("__synthetic")
    assert sensor_part({**SENSOR, "channel": 6}) != sensor_part(SENSOR)
    assert sensor_part(None) is None
    with pytest.raises(CalibrationError):
        sensor_key({}, "x")


def _result(placement="lab", synthetic=False, sensor=SENSOR):
    s = CalibrationSession(placement, DURATIONS)
    run_all(s, Feeder(s, synthetic=synthetic), SEPARABLE)
    r = dict(s.result)
    r["sensor"] = sensor
    r["synthetic"] = synthetic
    r["key"] = sensor_key(sensor, placement, synthetic)
    return r


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def real_result():
    return _result()


def test_store_round_trip_and_matching(tmp_path, real_result):
    store = CalibrationStore(tmp_path / "calibration")
    path = store.save(real_result)
    assert path.name == "lab__classic_1a0000000000_ch11-2_len128.json"
    loaded = store.load(real_result["key"])
    assert loaded["thresholds"] == real_result["thresholds"]
    assert loaded["baseline"]["mean_profile"] == real_result["baseline"]["mean_profile"]
    listing = store.list()
    assert [c["key"] for c in listing] == [real_result["key"]]
    assert store.find_match(SENSOR, synthetic=False)["key"] == real_result["key"]
    assert store.find_match({**SENSOR, "channel": 6}, synthetic=False) is None
    assert store.find_match(SENSOR, synthetic=True) is None
    for bad in ("../x", "a/b", "", "X Y", "..", 5):
        with pytest.raises(CalibrationError):
            store.load(bad)
    store.delete(real_result["key"])
    assert store.list() == []


def _write_log(path, n=600, rate=100.0, perturb=0.0):
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        for i, (ts, amps) in enumerate(stream(n, rate_hz=rate, noise=0.4, perturb=perturb, seed=3)):
            f.write(classic_line(amps, seq=i % 65536, ts_us=int(i * 1e6 / rate)) + "\n")


def _engine_with_manager(tmp_path):
    eng = Engine()
    mgr = CalibrationManager(eng, CalibrationStore(tmp_path / "calibration"))
    return eng, mgr


def test_auto_load_matching_calibration(tmp_path, real_result):
    CalibrationStore(tmp_path / "calibration").save(real_result)
    log = tmp_path / "gen.txt"
    _write_log(log)
    eng, mgr = _engine_with_manager(tmp_path)
    try:
        eng.start(ReplaySource(log, speed=0))
        assert eng.join(10)
        snap = eng.snapshot()
        assert snap["calibration"]["key"] == real_result["key"]
        assert snap["calibration"]["active"] is True
        assert snap["calibration"]["auto_loaded"] is True
        assert snap["thresholds"]["calibrated"] is True
        assert snap["thresholds"]["movement"] == real_result["thresholds"]["movement"]
        assert snap["motion"]["calibrated"] is True
        assert mgr.last_auto["action"] == "loaded"
    finally:
        eng.stop()


def test_synthetic_calibration_not_auto_applied_to_real_source(tmp_path):
    synth = _result(synthetic=True)
    # same sensor and placement, but computed from synthetic data
    store = CalibrationStore(tmp_path / "calibration")
    store.save(synth)
    log = tmp_path / "gen.txt"
    _write_log(log)
    eng, mgr = _engine_with_manager(tmp_path)
    try:
        eng.start(ReplaySource(log, speed=0))
        assert eng.join(10)
        snap = eng.snapshot()
        assert snap["calibration"]["key"] is None
        assert snap["calibration"]["active"] is False
        assert snap["thresholds"]["calibrated"] is False
        with pytest.raises(CalibrationError, match="SYNTHETIC"):
            mgr.load(synth["key"])
    finally:
        eng.stop()


def test_mismatched_calibration_cleared_on_new_sensor(tmp_path, real_result):
    other = dict(real_result)
    other["sensor"] = {**SENSOR, "channel": 6}
    other["key"] = sensor_key(other["sensor"], "lab")
    store = CalibrationStore(tmp_path / "calibration")
    store.save(other)
    log = tmp_path / "gen.txt"
    _write_log(log)
    eng, mgr = _engine_with_manager(tmp_path)
    try:
        res = mgr.load(other["key"])                       # manual load before any source: allowed
        assert res["key"] == other["key"]
        assert eng.calibration_info["key"] == other["key"]
        eng.start(ReplaySource(log, speed=0))
        assert eng.join(10)
        assert eng.calibration_info is None                # channel 11 data: does not match channel 6
        assert mgr.last_auto["action"] == "cleared"
    finally:
        eng.stop()


def test_manager_full_flow_with_engine(tmp_path):
    """Calibration driven by the engine thread from a replayed generated log."""
    log = tmp_path / "cal.txt"
    rate = 100.0
    with open(log, "w") as f:
        i = 0
        for key, secs in (("empty_baseline", 16), ("walking", 6), ("standing_still", 6), ("sitting", 6)):
            for ts, amps in stream(int(secs * rate), rate_hz=rate, seed=i, **SEPARABLE[key]):
                f.write(classic_line(amps, seq=i % 65536) + "\n")
                i += 1
    eng, mgr = _engine_with_manager(tmp_path)
    try:
        mgr.start("Test bench", DURATIONS)
        with pytest.raises(CalibrationError, match="no data source"):
            mgr.step_start()
        # a raw log replays at line_rate_hz (100 lines/s) scaled by speed; 20x keeps the timing
        eng.start(ReplaySource(log, speed=20.0, line_rate_hz=rate))
        mgr.step_start()
        assert mgr.state()["session"]["state"] == "recording"
        assert eng.join(15)
        state = mgr.state()["session"]
        assert state["steps"][0]["status"] == "done", state["steps"][0]
        assert state["steps"][0]["frames"] > 100
    finally:
        eng.stop()


def test_manager_save_load_delete(tmp_path):
    eng, mgr = _engine_with_manager(tmp_path)
    mgr.start("Bedroom", DURATIONS)
    with pytest.raises(CalibrationError, match="nothing to save"):
        mgr.save()
    s = mgr.session
    run_all(s, Feeder(s), SEPARABLE)
    assert s.state == "computed"
    saved = mgr.save()
    assert saved["key"] == "bedroom__classic_1a0000000000_ch11-2_len128"
    assert (tmp_path / "calibration" / (saved["key"] + ".json")).is_file()
    assert eng.calibration_info["key"] == saved["key"]
    assert eng.config.thresholds.calibrated is True
    assert mgr.state()["session"]["state"] == "saved"
    assert [c["key"] for c in mgr.store.list()] == [saved["key"]]
    mgr.clear()
    assert eng.calibration_info is None and eng.config.thresholds.calibrated is False
    mgr.load(saved["key"])
    assert eng.processor.baseline is not None
    mgr.delete(saved["key"])
    assert eng.calibration_info is None and mgr.store.list() == []
    assert np.isfinite(eng.config.thresholds.movement)

class GatedReplay(ReplaySource):
    """Replay that waits for ``gate`` before emitting (deterministic step start)."""

    def __init__(self, path, gate, **kw):
        super().__init__(path, **kw)
        self.gate = gate

    def lines(self):
        self.status.connected = True
        self.gate.wait(10)
        yield from super().lines()


def test_manager_full_flow_with_engine(tmp_path):
    """Calibration driven by the engine thread from a replayed generated log."""
    log = tmp_path / "cal.txt"
    rate = 100.0
    with open(log, "w") as f:
        i = 0
        for key, secs in (("empty_baseline", 18), ("walking", 8)):
            for ts, amps in stream(int(secs * rate), rate_hz=rate, seed=i, **SEPARABLE[key]):
                f.write(classic_line(amps, seq=i % 65536) + "\n")
                i += 1
    eng, mgr = _engine_with_manager(tmp_path)
    gate = threading.Event()
    try:
        mgr.start("Test bench", DURATIONS)
        with pytest.raises(CalibrationError, match="no data source"):
            mgr.step_start()
        # speed=0: emitted as fast as possible but host timestamps keep the
        # original 100 lines/s timeline, so packet-time step durations hold.
        eng.start(GatedReplay(log, gate, speed=0, line_rate_hz=rate))
        mgr.step_start()
        assert mgr.state()["session"]["state"] == "recording"
        gate.set()
        assert eng.join(15)
        state = mgr.state()["session"]
        assert state["steps"][0]["status"] == "done", state["steps"][0]
        assert state["steps"][0]["ok_frames"] >= 140
        # the source ended during the next step's wait -> walking not started yet
        assert state["current_step"] == "walking" and state["state"] == "ready"
    finally:
        gate.set()
        eng.stop()
